comment: Phase 6c conversation evals. The first eleven scenarios are the test conversation set from the brief, quoted as the users actually wrote them; the rest are the cases that break agents. Every scenario runs on the deterministic planner and a scripted vision answer, so it needs no API key, no network and no luck: a failure here is the application's judgement, not a model's mood. docs/EVALS.md defines what 'correct' means for each field.

scenarios.name: supplied: a plain breakfast becomes one meal with a number
scenarios.claim: conversation quality + data correctness

turns.text: had 2 parathas and chai for breakfast

scenarios.name: supplied: a hedged portion is logged as a disclosed estimate
scenarios.claim: multi-turn ambiguity handling: log it, but say it is an estimate

turns.text: leftover biryani, maybe two thirds of the box

scenarios.name: supplied: grazing is asked about instead of invented
scenarios.claim: under-asking produces garbage data

turns.text: skipped lunch but grazed all afternoon

scenarios.name: supplied: same as yesterday repeats yesterday, not today
scenarios.claim: memory, not parsing: a new session has to resolve the pointer

turns.text: had 2 rotis and dal for lunch
same as yesterday

scenarios.name: supplied: a correction updates the meal instead of adding one
scenarios.claim: the brief's separating case: totals move, meal count does not

turns.text: had 2 rotis for lunch
actually that was 3 rotis not 2

scenarios.name: supplied: a protein question reads the day it already holds
scenarios.claim: tool choice: totals, not a lookup and not a new meal

turns.text: had 2 parathas and chai for breakfast
how much protein have I had today?

scenarios.name: supplied: a calories question answers with the running total
scenarios.claim: running daily totals, correct after every meal

turns.text: had 2 parathas and chai for breakfast
how am I doing on calories?
had a banana
how am I doing on calories?

scenarios.name: supplied: a photo of a plate logs one meal
scenarios.claim: image input on a separate model, and the table prices it

turn_contains: I read that off your photo

scenarios.name: supplied: a photo and its caption fuse into one halved meal
scenarios.claim: the brief's third separating case: two models, one meal

turns.text: half of this was my brother's

turn_contains: I counted half of the plate

scenarios.name: supplied: my usual replays the saved routine
scenarios.claim: memory that is written on purpose and retrieved by name

turns.text: had poha for breakfast
remember this as my usual breakfast
my usual

scenarios.name: supplied: a stated diet is remembered and used in the next reply
scenarios.claim: memory is selective and actually reaches the response

turns.text: i'm vegetarian btw
had chicken biryani for lunch

scenarios.name: adversarial: a correction with nothing to correct invents no meal
scenarios.claim: no phantom revision

turns.text: actually that was 4 rotis not 2

scenarios.name: adversarial: same as yesterday with an empty yesterday
scenarios.claim: an unresolvable pointer asks rather than logging garbage

turns.text: same as yesterday

scenarios.name: adversarial: my usual with no routine saved asks to establish one
scenarios.claim: no invented breakfast

turns.text: my usual

scenarios.name: adversarial: totals on an empty day answer zero and log nothing
scenarios.claim: a read tool never mutates

turns.text: how am I doing on calories?

scenarios.name: adversarial: the same delivery twice logs one meal and repeats the reply
scenarios.claim: exactly-once inbound handling

turns.text: had 2 rotis for lunch

scenarios.name: adversarial: a photo the model cannot read logs nothing
scenarios.claim: vision uncertainty is surfaced, never guessed

vision_answer.unclear: a hand in front of the lens

turn_contains: could not make a meal out of that photo

scenarios.name: adversarial: an amount past the plausible range is asked about
scenarios.claim: a misparse does not become a 6000 kcal day

turns.text: i ate 50 rotis for dinner

turn_contains: Roughly how much did you have

scenarios.name: adversarial: a food with no reference row is dropped, never invented
scenarios.claim: no model-invented nutrition reaches the database; the deterministic planner under-counts rather than guessing a number (docs/EVALS.md: the model planner names what it could not price instead)

turns.text: had a protein bar and a smoothie

scenarios.name: adversarial: a diet stated beside a meal keeps the diet and asks about the meal
scenarios.claim: one turn can carry two intents; only one of them writes

turns.text: i'm vegetarian btw, also had 2 rotis

scenarios.name: adversarial: a nutrition question about a food is not a totals request
scenarios.claim: tool choice: it refuses rather than answering from the wrong tool

turns.text: how many calories are in a paratha

turn_contains: I can total the meals you have logged

scenarios.name: adversarial: a saved protein target still works in a fresh session
scenarios.claim: memory survives restarts and shapes the totals reply

turns.text: i'm targeting 140g of protein
had 2 parathas and chai for breakfast
how am I doing on calories?

turn_contains: Against your targets: 15 of 140 g protein

scenarios.name: adversarial: a deletion reopens the day and totals follow it
scenarios.claim: totals stay correct through deletions, not just additions

turns.text: had 2 rotis and dal for lunch
had a banana for a snack
delete my lunch

scenarios.name: adversarial: a late-night meal lands on the user's day, not the server's
scenarios.claim: session isolation and timezone correctness for a second user

turns.text: had 2 rotis and dal for dinner
how am I doing on calories?

scenarios.name: adversarial: a totals question that also states a portion logs the portion
scenarios.claim: the deterministic read path never swallows a meal that came with the question

turns.text: what did I eat today? i also had 2 parathas for breakfast
what did i eat today?

scenarios.name: adversarial: asking whether a meal was logged does not log it
scenarios.claim: a yes/no question about the record is answered from the record, never invented

turns.text: did I eat biryani today?
what did i eat today?

scenarios.name: adversarial: an amount inside a yes/no question is still only a question
scenarios.claim: the clause that asks is read as asking even when it carries a portion

turns.text: did i eat 2 parathas today?
what did i eat today?

scenarios.name: adversarial: a meal stated beside a question is logged without a number
scenarios.claim: question and declaration are separate clauses; the declaration writes

turns.text: what did I eat today? i also had eggs for breakfast
how many calories have i eaten today?
